title: Prompt Signal Greenhouse — scratch
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal playground for composing small prompt families and capturing brittle failure modes. Not a canonical library yet — just the greenhouse where weird seedlings live.

Notes to self / vibes:
- keep examples tiny (token budget) but representative of edge semantics
- write down negative examples explicitly (what I expect model to NOT do)
- prefer role prompts + one-shot behavior shaping over long static manuals (trying to exploit Redwood runtime caching and cheap KV reuse)
- track which model + config produced the behavior (hosted vs dedicated; quantized variant) – helps root cause: kernel selection vs generation policy

Active areas to test:
1) Instruction deflation: short instruction + exemplars vs long instruction + no exemplars\2) Temporal consistency: ask same question phrased across tenses, expect same entity linking\3) Few-shot ordering: canon fewshot set vs randomized ordering impacts on hallucination\4) Budgeted chain-of-thought: reduce token waste while preserving reasoning steps

Experimental templates (iterables):
- TEMPLATE A (role + constraint):
  You are an assistant that MUST answer in exactly two sentences. Do not include examples or sources.
  Q: {question}
  => expected: concise, no bullet lists, no hedging. Negative: enumerations, sources, adjectives like "probably"

- TEMPLATE B (few-shot pair set, 3 shots):
  Shot 1: Q: "Convert to YAML: list of env vars for staging app" A: <short YAML>
  Shot 2: Q: "Short summary of API error causes" A: <2-sentence>
  Shot 3: Q: "Explain HTTP 429 simply" A: <1-sentence>
  Prompt head: "Following examples show desired brevity and code-only responses. Now answer: {question}"

- TEMPLATE C (counterfactual anchoring):
  "Assume X is false. Given that, answer: {question}. If assumption contradicts evidence, state 'contradiction' and stop."

Few-shot bank (examples I used in runs):
- EX1 Q: "How to revoke API key in AWS console?" A: 3-step terse list (revoke->delete -> rotate)
- EX2 Q: "Write a curl example to call /v1/embeddings" A: code block only, no commentary
- EX3 Q: "Summarize PR #1023 in two lines" A: discrete bullet lines (but we avoid bullets in some templates)

Observed failure modes (catalog):
- soft-hedging: even with MUST instruction, model often prepends "I might be wrong" when prompt verbose
- hallucinated endpoints: invents non-existent flags in curl example when fewshot set skews to third-party libs
- sequence leak: model reproduces instruction examples verbatim instead of applying transformation when shot formatting too similar to query (format overfitting)
- token-bloat: chain-of-thought probes expand into long paraphrases; need forced step-count limit

Quick experiments to run (priority order):
- E1: Test Template A on 4 model variants: hosted-standard, hosted-quant4, dedicated-v2, dedicated-llm-8bit. Record: tokens in/out, latency, surprising phrases (list).
- E2: Randomize order of 3-shot Template B across 30 queries; measure hallucination rate against ground truth checklist.
- E3: Inject explicit STOP token marker (e.g., "<END>") and see if streaming + token-saver on Redwood runtime reliably truncates.

Measurement plan / rubric (quick):
- brevity_score: target <= 40 tokens for code answers, <= 25 tokens for 2-sentence answers
- hallucination_flag: yes/no compared to small oracle or quick wiki-check
- conformity: whether model violated top-level instruction (MUST / EXACTLY)
- latency buckets: <50ms, 50-200ms, >200ms (p95 measured on dedicated)

Run log snippets (seed runs):
- run_2024-11-15_A1: model hosted-standard, Template A, q: "List docker run flags to map port 3000" -> output included extraneous note "you might also consider" (conformity fail)
- run_2025-01-22_B3: dedicated-v2, Template B shuffled -> hallucinated config key 'max_retries' (not present in oracle), hallucination_flag=yes
- run_2025-03-04_E3: hosted-quant4 streaming with <END> marker -> stream cut correctly but left trailing punctuation at end-of-stream (post-process trim needed)

Hypotheses / interventions to try:
- explicit negative examples: include one-shot "Don't do X" where X is the common failure, placed before query to bias away
- format contrast: show both correct and wrong examples and label them (EXAMPLE: GOOD / BAD) — see if contrastive labeling reduces format overfitting
- token-budget clamp: use Redwood Optimize suggestion to reduce max_tokens + increase temperature stability to avoid verbose rationale
- forced-step limiter: ask for "List steps (max 3)" and include a 3-shot where each had 3 steps exactly

To-dos / next actions (personal):
- [ ] script E1/E2 runs into prompt-harness (PR reference above) and log structured CSV for signal tracking
- [ ] add small watch dashboard in Console per-route to surface conformity regressions (hook to rollouts)
- [ ] convert best-performing Template A into a lightweight library entry once stable for 5 runs
- [ ] cross-check Template C results against Canary model with KV cache turned off to rule out state leakage

Open questions (unresolved):
- does dedicated quantized variant behave systematically different on format overfitting vs hosted? (kernel selection hypothesis)
- can we rely on explicit <END> markers across streaming backends, or do we need server-side truncation?
- are there prompt constructs that reliably reduce hallucination for short code outputs without increasing tokens?

Related links / quick references (for me):
- slack: #prompt-experiments thread: "thread:prompt-greenhouse"
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-harness/pull/198 (run harness for banked experiments)
- Confluence: Prompt Library Index (linked above)

Rough archival note:
If something stabilizes, move into shared_drives/product/hosted-api/prompt-library as a named template + small evaluation notes. For now, keep messy and iterate fast.

Random scratch (don’t delete):
- micro-template: "Assistant: Answer in N words. Example: \"{ex}\". Now: {q}" — test with N=10, models tend to go 2-3 words over consistently.

End of greenhouse scratch.
